title: Not Wanting Another Man’s Wife
note: This is not wanting another man’s wife through the delusion of desire. It follows good conduct because it is found only in those who have good conduct.

couplets.plain: The folly of chasing a woman who is another man’s property is not found in those who know righteousness and wealth.
couplets.pm: The ignorance of loving and pursuing a woman who is another man’s property isn’t found in those on earth who have studied the books of righteousness and of wealth. Those who study the books of pleasure, and look to pleasure alone, even give this wicked conduct a name, so he names only the two. Those with this folly have neither righteousness nor wealth.
couplets.sensitive: speaks of a wife as her husband’s property

links.quote: The folly of chasing a woman who is another man’s property
links.reason: Calls the pursuit a folly that anyone who knows righteousness and wealth avoids.

couplets.plain: Of all who stand outside righteousness, none is a greater fool than those who stand at another man’s door.
couplets.pm: Of all who stand in sin because of desire, none are as foolish as those who love another man’s wife and stand at his door. Sinners who follow women, or go with prostitutes or women of low family, lose righteousness and wealth. Those at another’s door lose even the pleasure they sought, through fear. So they have no pleasure either.

links.quote: those who stand at another man’s door
links.reason: Ranks the man waiting at another’s door the greatest fool among all wrongdoers.

couplets.plain: Those who do evil in the home of someone who trusts them are surely no different from the dead.
couplets.pm: Those who like to sin with the wife of a man who doesn’t suspect them are dead, though they have life. They are no different from the dead because their souls gain none of righteousness, wealth and pleasure. “One who trusts” is said because they can do this only through the husband’s trust.

links.quote: do evil in the home of someone who trusts them
links.reason: Makes it a betrayal of trust as well, since the one wronged suspects nothing.

links.quote: are surely no different from the dead
links.reason: For anyone drawn to the spouse of someone who trusts them: this makes them no better than dead.

couplets.plain: However great you may be, what good is it, if you enter another man’s home without a millet seed’s worth of thought?
couplets.pm: However great someone is, what does it come to if, in the delusion of desire, they enter another man’s home without weighing their fault even by a millet seed? Like Indra, they lose all greatness and fall low. Some take “not weighing” with the other man, as the husband who suspects nothing.

links.quote: what good is it, if you enter another man’s home

couplets.plain: Whoever trespasses on a home, thinking it easy, earns blame that will never die.
couplets.pm: One who thinks “It is easy” and, with no thought of what follows, trespasses on another’s home earns a blame on his family that stands for all time and never dies. To trespass on a home is to cross the line with the wife of the house.

links.quote: earns blame that will never die

couplets.plain: Enmity, sin, fear and blame: these four never leave the one who trespasses on a home.
couplets.pm: Enmity, sin, fear and blame on his family: these four faults never leave the man who crosses the line with another’s wife. So he loses both worlds. These six couplets tell the fault in one who wants another’s wife.

links.reason: Enmity heads the four things that will not leave him.

links.quote: never leave the one who trespasses on a home

couplets.plain: The one who doesn’t crave the womanhood of a woman who is another’s is the one called a householder who lives by righteousness.
couplets.pm: The one called a householder, living with righteousness as his nature, is the man who doesn’t want the womanhood of one who belongs to another and stays in his ways. Only he is said to practise household righteousness.

links.quote: doesn’t crave the womanhood of a woman who is another’s
links.reason: Makes not craving another’s wife the test of a good man at home.

links.quote: called a householder who lives by righteousness

couplets.plain: The great manhood that won’t look at another’s wife is, for the worthy, not only righteousness but full conduct.
couplets.pm: The great manhood that doesn’t hold another’s wife in mind is, for the worthy, both righteousness and complete conduct. Even men who can defeat outer enemies find it hard to subdue desire, the enemy within, so this is called great manhood. Merely not doing this wrong brings both, which are otherwise hard to do.

links.quote: The great manhood that won’t look at another’s wife
links.reason: Not so much as looking at her is both righteousness and full conduct.

couplets.plain: Who in this world ringed by the fearsome sea deserves every good? Those who don’t embrace the shoulders of a woman who is another’s.
couplets.pm: Who in the world ringed by the fearsome sea is fit to gain every good? Those who don’t join the shoulders of a woman who belongs to another. The sea is fearsome because its width, depth and contents can’t be measured. They gain good in both worlds.

links.quote: Those who don’t embrace the shoulders of a woman who is another’s
links.reason: Reserves every good thing for those who keep from her embrace.

couplets.plain: Even if you keep no bounds of righteousness and do wrong, it is good not to crave the womanhood of one within another’s bounds.
couplets.pm: Even if a man doesn’t make righteousness his own and does sinful things, if he doesn’t want the womanhood of one within another’s bounds, that is good. This quality alone will stand out. These four couplets tell the quality of one who doesn’t want another’s wife.

links.quote: it is good not to crave the womanhood of one within another’s bounds
Even if you keep no bounds of righteousness and do wrong

ideaLinks.reason: Enmity is one of the four things that never leave the one who trespasses.
